Distinct nonconstant affine forms define the full-dimensional arrangement cells via closures, so the cells cover R^d and share boundary faces. Including every genuine formula-change facet ensures f is affine on each cell.

The affine-piece identities are finite coefficientwise linear equalities. Their facet restrictions provide continuity; nonnegative jump coefficients give nonnegative directional slope jumps along every generic crossing line, hence global convexity by continuity.

The common C witness is correct for any fixed scaling and orientation of the affine forms: G has jump coefficient C and H=G-f has C-delta_ij >= 0. Both are affine on each arrangement cell and their restrictions satisfy all constraints.
The no-fold case is covered by C=0 and an empty sum: f is affine, G=0, H=-f.
The suggested objective sum(lambda_ij+mu_ij) is nonnegative on the nonempty feasible polyhedron and therefore has a finite attained LP optimum; no arbitrary-objective boundedness claim is made.

The facetwise equalities are an equivalent reformulation of the source construction on the refined arrangement, with an explicit feasibility witness; they do not require the omitted Farkas formulation or old partition notation.
